AUTHOR: Zouin
TITLE: Improving CNN Fish Detection and Classification with Tracking
REGION: New Caledonia, South Pacific (deep slopes and seamounts, 47-552 m)
SPECIES: Deep-water snappers (Lutjanidae): Pristipomoides filamentosus, P. flavipinnis, P. argyrogrammicus, Aphareus rutilans, Aprion virescens, Etelis coruscans, Parapristipomoides squamimaxillaris
DATA: Own deep BRUVS footage (GoPro Hero 4, 1920x1080, 60 fps, LED light): 289 fifteen-second videos; 3521 training images
V_EV: Sec. 2: 'a 1200 lumens, 120-degree angle led light' and 'recorded at depths varying between 47 and 552 m'; turbidity mentioned only as a generic limitation (Sec. 6)
D_EV: Sec. 2: 'split into a training set of 159 (Table 1) videos ... and a testing dataset made of 130 videos ... ensured that the testing and training datasets were independent'
R_EV: Sec. 2: single dataset of 289 videos 'recorded on deep slopes and seamounts marine habitats of New-Caledonia'
C_EV: Sec. 3.7: 'we perform a post-processing step to eliminate potentially erroneous IDs ... If two bounding boxes exhibit a significant overlap exceeding a selected IoU threshold'; Appendix A 'Detection Threshold: 0.5'
E_EV: Sec. 3.8: 'To evaluate the accuracy of our algorithm, we calculated F1-Scores for each species' (precision/recall/F1/detection accuracy only; no count or MaxN compared)
ARCH: Faster R-CNN Inception-ResNet-V2 (1024x1024, TensorFlow) + OpenCV legacy tracker with timeout frames (20), forward and reverse tracking, IoU-based ID merging and majority-class relabelling
METR: Per-species precision, recall, F1 (avg F1 0.791 -> 0.846), detection accuracy TP/(TP+FP+FN) 62.3% -> 73.3%, processing time
NOTE: Video-level split explicitly motivated by independence of train/test (D4 = Y) but leakage not analysed; D3 = N (no near-duplicate removal; test frames at 30 fps). '12% more individuals detected' refers to recall of bounding boxes, not a validated count against human MaxN, so E1 = 없음. C5 coded as duplicate-ID handling (IoU merging of overlapping tracks); no human-verified false-positive rate. Species list in Tables 1/2 is garbled by pdftotext duplication; 7 species in training, 6 evaluated in Tables 3-5 (P. squamimaxillaris absent from test tables). Hyperparameters (threshold 0.5, timeout 20, IoU 0.35) in Appendix A, no sensitivity analysis.
